delta.summary: I built a new character from my demonology research - Dante and Milton, Dostoevsky's Demons, Asmodeus, Sakhr, the Shamir - the priest of the Chronotopium, keeper of the Noiseless Labor.

I stated how the novels work: each has two layers, the fictional project and its mythical layer - and the Chronotopium's cosmology is versions, many versions coexisting and conflicting. The characters gather and audit the text I am writing; the trilogy ascends in dimensions: historiogenesis, archivogenesis, algorithmogenesis.

I ruled on the History-Project audit until every variance had my word: the syntheses are kept, historiophany is coeval, Viktor is the psychiatrist, Messenger-Boy is an office, the Priest of St-Elsewhere is a form of the Baron, Maud/MOD is a modular being. And the cosmology generates the characters - that generation is the Abstract Characterology.

aesthetic.problem: A log structure that is at once human (.MD) and machine-readable (NDJSON/JSONL, append-only), distributed across the workspace, tied to the version history - and qualitative, an aesthetic operation, not a metric.
aesthetic.tension: Structure enough to query and to chain to commit hashes; openness enough to hold qualia, aesthetic problems and provenance without flattening them.
aesthetic.solution: Two separate streams, .MD and .JSONL, complementary - neither the source of the other - interlocked by timestamps, by shared vocabularies, by citeable record ids, and by the same qualitative content.
aesthetic.elegance: The interlock is contextual, not mechanical: the same event lived once, recorded twice, each form doing what only it can do.
aesthetic.status: format taken for now, at the operator's word; terms remain proposals until ratified
